title: Shmashan mein Mahavira Swami ko Yaksha ne kaise pariksha di?
hooks: Shmashan ki raat... Mahavira Swami kayotsarga mein.
Ek Yaksha aaya, unki samta todne — kya hua?
Raat bhar aag, bhoot, sher... Swami hile tak nahi.
hook_why: Opens with named entity (Mahavira Swami) and place (shmashan) in first 4 words — matches raaz hook rule. Visual of meditating idol in cremation ground creates immediate kinetic curiosity without audio.
metaphor: A single white marble idol standing unmoved while illusions (fire, ghosts, beasts) swirl around like smoke — the still center proves inner victory.
mechanism: Yaksha creates illusion of fire to test fear
Mahavira's kayotsarga remains unbroken — fire cannot touch inner stillness
Ghost army appears with terrifying sounds — tests attachment to safety
Single-pointed gaze (drishti) dissolves illusions — no reaction, no flinch
Wild animals (lion, snake, elephant) approach — test instinctive survival fear
Each beast fades like mist — proves they were mental projections
Yaksha reveals true divine form — acknowledges victory of samta
Declares 'Samkitva jeeta, moh haar gaya' — right faith conquers delusion
Lesson: true tapasya is internal equanimity, not external austerity

claims.claim: Mahavira Swami stayed in a cremation ground (shmashan) during his ascetic period and was tested by a Yaksha.
claims.basis: Kalpasutra (Lives of the Jinas) by Bhadrabahu — contains biography of Mahavira including his 12 years of asceticism and trials.

claims.claim: The Yaksha created illusions of fire, ghosts, and wild animals to disturb Mahavira's meditation.
claims.basis: Kalpasutra account of Mahavira's trials (pariksha) during kayotsarga in shmashan.

claims.claim: Mahavira remained unmoved in kayotsarga (standing meditation) throughout all tests.
claims.basis: Kalpasutra — central theme of samta (equanimity) as highest tap.

claims.claim: The Yaksha finally revealed his true form, bowed, and declared 'Samkitva jeeta, moh haar gaya' (Right faith won, delusion lost).
claims.basis: Kalpasutra narrative of Yaksha's submission after witnessing unshakable samta.

claims.claim: Source is Kalpasutra, ascribed to Acharya Bhadrabahu, a Cheda Sutra of Shvetambara canon.
claims.basis: Wikipedia, Wisdom Library, Hinduwebsite.com — all confirm Kalpasutra authorship and content.
